components.gap: Durrett (pp. 16-17, PDF pp. 24-25) defines almost sure convergence as P(Omega_o)=1 for the convergence set Omega_o={lim_n X_n exists} with no prescribed limit, uses the convention X_inf=limsup_n X_n to obtain a limit on the whole space, and defines extended random variables as functions whose domain is a set D in F with values in R*=[-inf,inf], measurable for the Borel sets of the order topology generated by [-inf,a), (a,b), (b,inf], noting that all earlier results then generalize. The handbook definition restricts every function to the whole of Omega (line 237), uses the sigma-algebra generated by [-inf,a] without stating or proving its identity with the Borel sets of that topology, and defines almost sure convergence only toward a specified real X (lines 317-319). The domain-D variant, the topological definition of the Borel sets of R*, convergence without a prescribed limit, and the X_inf convention are absent from the route.
